# Binary stream from `stream/`

The twelve images `stream/bruxus_1.png` to `stream/bruxus_12.png` each show rows of binary digits. Reading left to right and top to bottom, image by image, gives one stream of 416 digits (images 1 to 11 have four 8-digit rows each; image 12 has four 16-digit rows).

## Stream

```

```

| Image | Rows, top to bottom |
|---|---|
| bruxus_1 | 01011010, 10100101, 00110011, 01001011 |
| bruxus_2 | 10100101, 01011010, 11001100, 10110100 |
| bruxus_3 | 00110101, 11001010, 01011100, 10100100 |
| bruxus_4 | 10000101, 10011010, 10111100, 11110100 |
| bruxus_5 | 10000100, 00011011, 10111100, 01110101 |
| bruxus_6 | 01111000, 11100100, 01000011, 10001010 |
| bruxus_7 | 00111000, 10100100, 00000011, 10001010 |
| bruxus_8 | 00101000, 10100100, 00000011, 10001010 |
| bruxus_9 | 00101100, 10100100, 00000111, 10001110 |
| bruxus_10 | 11101100, 11101100, 11001111, 11001110 |

| bruxus_12 | 0000011111101010, 0000011111101011, 0000011111101100, 0000011111101101 |

## Verification

The stream was read by eye and then independently by machine (Tesseract OCR on each detected row, limited to the characters 0 and 1). Both readings agree on all 416 digits.

## Interpretation

Not yet decided. The stream is 52 bytes. Read as ASCII bytes it is not plain text, and the last four 16-bit rows are the values 2026, 2027, 2028 and 2029 in binary.
